contents.entry: Shared needs: what the shared author declares for this node
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
State paths and their cleanup scripts
The look: the style the atlas must carry

pointers.sibling: Input and output record schemas of this node
pointers.principle: Rule 3 (three attempts then report) and rule 4 (artifacts under the state root); the atlas builds from a record, never from a person
Atomic rename into a hash-named directory; sprite.sheet keyed by hash; duplicate put replayed as 200
pointers.needs: The shared anchors this volume relies on, declared as needs until shared/ lands

in.record: art inventory record (built from the companion table and the originals folder)
suite.plan entry art for a commit touching tools/map/art/** (shared need: planner mapping)

shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares, using the anchor name of the node that owns the thing (envelope and cas from N-01, record-kinds-registry from N-18, codes from N-43, break-glass from N-27). check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for art.building 100; art.superseded 200; art.built 201; art.gap 300; art.rejected 422; art.failed 500. Owner-acts: art.gap (an originals ticket is cut as data, the placeholder sprite ships meanwhile).
The record envelope every kind carries: id, at (UTC), code, kind, node, attempt where one applies; this node reads and writes records only inside it.
idempotency(key PRIMARY KEY, seq, response JSON, at); a seen key replays its response with code 200.

The record kinds registry (every kind with its code set, writer node and schema path, loaded by N-43 with the code table) carries the kinds this node reads and writes: art.inventory, sprite.sheet (keyed by atlas sha256), art.gap, suite.plan (entry art), pod.run (N-24).
The suite planner maps a commit touching tools/map/art/** to a suite.plan entry named art, so this node starts from a record and never from a person running the atlas build.
The pod runner's retry ladder (3 attempts, backoff) is the only retry for the atlas build; a 422 art.rejected is never retried because the input, not the infrastructure, is wrong.
No cog: every wait has a timeout and a fallback, nothing starts by an agent typing, no agent is a gate; the system drives (brief C rule 3).
Many agents at once from the first line: append-only records, compare-and-swap, idempotent retryable steps, conflicts that report as 409 (brief C rule 2).
Every automated step retries up to 3 times with backoff, then recovers and reports as a record; a dead record becomes exactly one card.
Every state path this node names lives under $COQ_STATE, never in the repository, and has a cleanup script registered with N-45 (brief C rule 6, C35).

purpose.s: Turn the art inventory into one sprite atlas the five screens draw from, with the attribution and license texts beside it, and make it impossible for a Wube-derived, BiusArt or unknown-origin file to ship.
The owner's bar: "1 to 1 factorio style and format" down to the images, original art, Krastorio 2 as the art direction (command-center-visual-bar; HANDOFF rulings 10 and 11).

The inventory's headline (section 1.3): Krastorio 2 has no safe belts, inserters, lamps, pipes, GUI frames, progress bars, ground tiles or alert pictograms; 260 class 1 high files have commit-level proof; 506 class 1 medium rest on the README statement. So the atlas is Krastor machines plus original pixel art for everything between them (section 5.6).

input.s: The art inventory record is built by tools/map/art/inventory.sh from two inputs: the companion table krastorio-art-inventory-files.tsv (one row per file with class, rule code and confidence) and the originals folder tools/map/art/original/ with its provenance file.
input.field: Every Krastorio2Assets path with class 1, plus the confidence (high or medium) and the sha256 of the file as cloned at Krastorio2Assets 96e5f05.

Every file under tools/map/art/original/ with its provenance entry: author seat or person, date UTC, tool, "drawn from scratch in the Factorio idiom", and the sprite group it fills (belts, inserters, lamps, pipes, ground, GUI frames, progress bars, status lights, alert pictograms, crates, ore).
Every class 2, 3 and 4 path and the 162 Wube graphics the K2 Lua references by path (section 3.5), so a later copy is caught by sha and by path.
Which class 1 confidence ships: high only, or high plus medium after a visual check (inventory section 7 question 1). Default high only until a ruling says otherwise.

output.s: One atlas build per art inventory record and policy: atlas.png (power-of-two sheets, 2048 x 2048 at most, several pages if needed), atlas.json (frame rectangles, pivot, animation frame counts from the K2 Lua, scale), ATTRIBUTION.txt, LICENSE-LGPL-3.0.txt, LICENSE-GPL-3.0.txt, PROVENANCE.json, and the status.
output.field: Hash of atlas.json plus every page, so a screen can pin the exact sheet it was tested against.
Every shipped sprite with its source: krastorio path and sha, or original path and provenance id.
201 built; 422 rejected naming the file and the rule that caught it; 500 after three failed builds.
output.s: No Wube-derived or BiusArt file: a build with any denylist hit is 422 and produces no atlas; the previous atlas keeps serving.

mechanism.diagram: flowchart LR T[krastorio-art-inventory-files.tsv] --> I[inventory.sh: allowlist, denylist, originals with provenance] O[tools/map/art/original/ plus PROVENANCE.json] --> I I --> V[verify.sh: sha256 of every candidate against allowlist, path and sha against denylist, provenance present] V -->|hit| R[422 art.rejected record, no atlas] V -->|clean| S[slice.py: crop, slice frames by K2 Lua counts, scale, pack] S --> A[atlas pages, atlas.json, ATTRIBUTION.txt, LICENSE texts] A --> C[201 sprite.sheet record with atlas_sha256] C --> M[screens N-38 to N-42 load the pinned atlas]

step.s: Reads the TSV copy that the repo pins by sha256 (tools/map/art/inventory.tsv.sha256 names the hash of the reference table; the table itself stays in the state root, outside the repo) and writes the art.inventory record as JSON to the work directory and to the store through the Go service's record.put when running on the host, or as a build artifact when running in a pod (a pod cannot reach the store, D23; the unit writes it to records/art.jsonl and N-24's artifact import puts it in the store for this node when the build ends, nodes/N-24/spec.xml#m-mirror, because the art suite entry lists art.inventory and sprite.sheet in its records, nodes/N-23/spec.xml#output).

For each file the atlas manifest names: a Krastorio file must match an allowlist row by path and sha256 at the stated confidence under the policy; an original must have a PROVENANCE.json entry; any denylist hit by sha or path is a 422 with the rule code quoted from the inventory (W1 to W9, B1, T1 to T11).

The verify step also greps the whole tools/map tree for Wube file names from the inventory's class 2 groups (for example express-transport-belt, pipe-covers, bulk-inserter) and for the 162 __base__ paths, so a stray copy under another folder fails too.

Runs with python3 -I inside the pinned build image. Crops the machine bodies and their shadow and reflection layers (inventory section 5.1), slices animation sheets by the frame counts read from the Krastorio2 Lua for that building, scales to the map's tile size (32 px per tile at 1x, 64 at 2x for the phone's device pixel ratio), and packs with a shelf packer into pages.
Change notice: the ATTRIBUTION.txt line per file says cropped, sliced, scaled and recompressed, as the inventory's proposed notice requires (section 6.3).

Original pixel art for belts (yellow with dark edges and moving chevrons), inserters (small yellow arms), lamps (round, off, green, amber, red, with glow), pipes (grey), ground tiles (dusty ochre to dark brown with a faint grid), crates, ore patches, GUI nine-slice frames, buttons, progress bars, status dots and alert pictograms, drawn as PNG at 1x and 2x plus the SVG source, in the style the reference README section 3 establishes.

Each original is a worker-seat ticket (N-16) with the sprite group and the reference frame named; a human or a tool may draw it, and the provenance entry names which. Nothing is traced from a Wube or K2 sprite; the verify step's silhouette check (48 x 48 alpha mask correlation against the local Factorio 2.0.77 install when present on the host, skipped in pods) catches a traced copy.

make -C tools/map art runs steps 1 to 3 and writes the atlas to $COQ_STATE/map/art/dist/<atlas_sha256>/; make -C tools/map build copies the pinned atlas into dist/ for the image (N-35) and for the bearings tier serving /board (N-48).

start.s: In CI: a commit touching tools/map/art/** maps to the art suite in the suite planner (N-23), which runs the pipeline as a pod (D22) and posts its result on the sha through the gate (N-25); the pod's art.inventory and sprite.sheet records reach the store through N-24's artifact import (nodes/N-24/spec.xml#m-mirror); an unmapped path plans the full set, so the art suite runs on any commit the planner cannot classify.
On the host: the Go service's daily tick (N-06) re-runs verify.sh against the current atlas, so a later change to the inventory table or the policy is caught without a commit.
No agent runs the slicer, the packer or the verify step by hand; a seat drawing an original commits files and nothing else.

wait.name: art-suite-pod
wait.fallback: pod.run exit with code 504, infrastructure retry by N-24's ladder, then 500 art.failed
wait.s: The pipeline over 260 to 766 files and the originals is measured on a Pi core at under four minutes; the bound is set from that measurement plus headroom and re-measured when the file count grows.

wait.name: reference-table-present
wait.s: The TSV is in the state root on the host and a CI artifact in the pod; if neither matches the pinned sha256, the build stops at once: a wrong inventory must never produce an atlas.

wait.name: factorio-install-for-silhouette-check
wait.fallback: skip the silhouette check and record 201 with check=skipped; the daily host tick runs it where the install exists
wait.s: The install at /mnt/d/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Factorio is host-only; the check is advisory in pods and binding on the host.

wait.name: originals-ticket
wait.fallback: the atlas ships at once with the gap filled by a plain placeholder sprite from tools/map/art/original/placeholder/ and the sprite.sheet record lists the gap
wait.s: A missing original never blocks the atlas; the Map screen draws the placeholder and the Alerts screen lists the gap as a 300 waiting record, so the owner sees the hole instead of a stalled build.

retries.s: An infrastructure failure of the pod (image pull, node loss, timeout) is retried by N-24's ladder up to 3 times; a verify failure (422) is never retried, because the input is wrong and a retry would produce the same answer (the same split as pod.run: an assertion failure is never retried).
After the third infrastructure failure the node writes 500 art.failed and N-28 builds one card; the last good atlas keeps serving from its pinned hash.

many-agents.s: Readers: a build seat reads #mechanism and #checklist; a drawing seat reads #look and the sprite group it was given; the reviewer reads #waits and this section.

Many drawing seats at once: each original is its own file set under tools/map/art/original/<group>/<name>.{png,svg,json}; the ticket declares those files and nothing else, so two seats never claim one sprite (N-14 refuses overlap). PROVENANCE.json is not one shared file: it is a directory of one JSON per sprite, merged by the inventory step, so no two tickets edit one file.

Atlas builds in parallel on two commits: each build writes to its own $COQ_STATE/map/art/work/<sha>/ and publishes to dist/<atlas_sha256>/ by rename after a complete write (atomic on one filesystem); two builds of the same content produce the same hash and the second rename finds the directory present and records 200 art.superseded without rewriting.
Store writes: the sprite.sheet record is keyed by atlas_sha256 with that hash as the idempotency key; a duplicate put is a no-op 409 at N-01 that the build reports as 200.

Screens never read the newest atlas by name; they read the hash pinned in the build they were tested with (N-37 binding check includes the atlas hash), so a new atlas cannot change a running page under the owner.

status-codes.code: The inventory record of a build, imported from the art suite's artifact (nodes/N-24/spec.xml#m-mirror).
An identical atlas already exists; nothing written.
Atlas, attribution, licenses and provenance written and hashed; screens may pin it.
A sprite group has no original yet and ships a placeholder; a drawing ticket is open.
A file failed origin verification; record names the file and the inventory rule; never retried; the committing ticket's PR is red through the gate.

state-paths.path: Scratch of one build: crops, slices, logs.

path.cleanup: tools/map/bin/cleanup.sh --art-dist --keep-pinned (keeps every hash a live tier or the current image pins, deletes the rest)
kept on purpose: the owner's data copy (reference README section 1); cleanup.sh lists it and refuses apply; only the owner removes it, by disposition

state-paths.path: Inventory report, table, screenshots, and the mods clones.

path.cleanup: N-45 retention class: keep every record (small, append-only)

state-paths.s: Nothing above lives in the repository; the repository holds the scripts, the originals with provenance, and the pinned sha256 of the inventory table.

look.requirement: owner: 1 to 1 factorio style and format down to the images; original art only
look.s: Machines: Krastor class 1 bodies with their shadow and reflection layers (inventory section 5.1): advanced chemical plant, advanced furnace, advanced assembling machine, matter plant, fuel refinery, research server, electrolysis plant, energy storage, quantum computer, greenhouse, wind turbine, roboports, storage tanks, warehouse, tesla coil, flare stack; each DAG node is assigned one body in tools/map/registry/machines.json (N-37).

Between the machines, original art in the reference README section 3 idiom: ground dusty ochre to dark brown with a faint grid; belts yellow with dark edges and moving chevrons; pipes grey; inserters small yellow arms; lamps the only saturated light (orange, red, green); blueprint ghosts as translucent blue outlines; nothing pure black or pure white.

GUI: nine-slice panels and buttons drawn from the vanilla values in inventory section 4.3 and 4.4 (panel #313031, inside shallow #403F40, deep #242324, caption #FFE6C0, orange #FAA838, glow #E1B16A, production green #2BE327, heat red #DA4535), corner 8 px, header 24 px, slot 40 px, button minimum 108 x 28; fonts Titillium Web (OFL) and IBM Plex Mono (OFL) shipped as web fonts.

Check: look-check.mjs renders the atlas sample page and compares panel and lamp pixels with the token table; verify.sh proves origin; the screenshot pair on the promotion record is read by the architect.

item.check: inventory.sh produces an art.inventory record from the pinned table and the originals, with allowlist, denylist and policy.
item.proof: The record JSON in the work directory and its sha256 of the table equal to tools/map/art/inventory.tsv.sha256.

item.check: verify.sh rejects a class 2 file by sha, a class 2 file by path, a class 3 file, a class 4 file and an original without provenance.
item.proof: Five test fixtures under tools/map/art/tests/ each producing 422 with the expected rule code, run in make -C tools/map test.

item.check: The atlas contains only allowlisted Krastorio files at the policy confidence and originals with provenance.
item.proof: PROVENANCE.json of the built atlas cross-checked by verify.sh with exit 0, saved beside the sprite.sheet record.

item.check: ATTRIBUTION.txt matches the inventory's section 6.3 text, lists every shipped Krastorio path, names contributors (HerptyDerpoty, Lars Pensjo, Caleb Heuer, DarkStarBuster, Anthony Edwards) where a file was first added by them, and LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 texts ship verbatim beside it.
item.proof: A diff of ATTRIBUTION.txt against the generated expectation and the two license files' sha256 against the FSF texts.

item.check: No Krastorio name or logo suggests endorsement; the K2 logo is not in the atlas unless the owner rules it in.
item.proof: verify.sh denylists buildings/logo/logo.png by default; a ruling record may lift it.

item.check: Originals exist for belts, inserters, lamps and pipes at 1x and 2x with SVG source.
item.proof: Directory listing under tools/map/art/original/{belts,inserters,lamps,pipes}/ and the sprite.sheet record with no 300 gap for those four groups.

item.check: The atlas is published by hash and pinned by the screens.
item.proof: The atlas_sha256 in the sprite.sheet record equals the hash in tools/map/registry/bindings.json (N-37).

item.check: The daily host tick re-verifies the current atlas.
item.proof: One daily verify record per day in the store for seven days.

item.check: Every state path has a cleanup script in the registry.
item.proof: N-45 entries and a dry-run listing.

permissions.s: Build seat: writes tools/map/art/*.sh, slice.py, tests, Makefile targets; never writes under original/.
Drawing seat: writes only tools/map/art/original/<group>/<name>.* and its provenance JSON; never touches scripts or the inventory hash.
No seat edits the reference folder in the state root; no seat copies any file out of the mods clones into the repository (reference README section 1 and section 5).
Policy change (high only to high plus medium) is a ruling record (N-29), never a config edit by a seat.

monitoring.s: The Map screen draws N-36 as a machine with the latest sprite.sheet code as its lamp and the last verify time as its heartbeat; a 300 gap shows as an amber lamp with the group named in the Machine screen.
A 422 on main (a bad file merged past the gate) is an alert record (N-41) and one card, because it means the gate did not run the art suite.

runbook.s: Build by hand for a test (reading and writing only the work directory): make -C tools/map art ART_POLICY=high.
Cleanup: tools/map/bin/cleanup.sh --art-work --older-than 7d; tools/map/bin/cleanup.sh --art-dist --keep-pinned; both list first and delete only with --apply.

Open questions the owner or a lawyer resolves by ruling, not by a seat (inventory section 7): the medium group, the 2019-11-11 pictograms, whether the LGPL grant covers a public page, the flib slots, the pre-optimisation originals.
